title: Development and validation of the questionnaire “Metacognitive ability to program activities”
abstract: Context and relevance. In modern social conditions, the problem of studying the metacognitive abilities and skills of an individual engaged in various activities remains relevant, as the degree of awareness of one's own thinking strategies and methods of achieving effectiveness can significantly influence both the success of an individual's activities and the overall success of their self-realization. Objective: to develop and test the validity and reliability of the questionnaire “Metacognitive Ability to Program Activities”, based on the understanding that the effectiveness of activities (educational and professional) is determined by the developed metacognitive abilities that allow an individual to timely assess and manage their own intentions and actions in order to achieve the goal of the activity. Methods and materials. The study involved 1785 participants (M = 20, SD = 1.9, 77% women and 23% men). To test the reliability of the questionnaire, the following methods were used: the Reflexivity Questionnaire by A.V. Karpov, the Self-Efficacy Questionnaire (by J. Maddox and M. Scheier, adapted by A.V. Boyarintseva), the General Self-Efficacy Scale (by R. Schwarzer and M. Jerusalem, adapted by V.G. Romek), the Self-Regulation Style Questionnaire (by V.I. Morosanova), and the Action Control Questionnaire (by J. Kuhl, adapted by S.A. Shapkin). Statistical data analysis was performed using the R programming language (v.4.3) in the RStudio environment (v. 2023.12.1+402 “Ocean Storm”). Reliability analysis (Cronbach's alpha) was conducted using the “ltm” package functions, and confirmatory factor analysis was implemented using the “lavaan” package functions. Graphical support was provided using the “semPlot”, “ggplot2”, and “patchwork” packages. Results. A questionnaire was developed and tested, the expediency of which was confirmed by a confirmatory factor analysis performed using the maximum likelihood method: GFI = 0.957, AGFI = 0.943, CFI = 0.971, TLI = 0.966, SRMR = 0.025, RMSEA = 0.049; checking the internal consistency of statements used in the questionnaire using the Kronbach coefficient, (α = 0.943), convergent validity (links were found between the metacognitive ability to program activities and reflexivity, indicators of the ability to self-regulate, types of self-efficacy and control over actions (in the field of implementation and failures), where r ≥ 0.138 at p < 0.0001, as well as a test of discriminant validity, which revealed the absence of correlations with an indicator not included in the construct under study (involuntary control over the action during planning)). Thus, construct validity can be considered pronounced. Conclusions. The tested questionnaire includes 18 items, rated on a 5-point Likert scale, which were developed based on the theoretical model of self-assessment of metacognitive behavior by D. LaCosta. The questionnaire can be used to analyze the formation of metacognitive ability to program activities, as an element of metacognitive awareness of an individual, its social and intellectual maturity, as well as the possibility of forecasting, based on its application, the potential success of mastering educational and professional activities.
